relatedSnapshot.title: Gmail sync is slowing the whole app: skip empty history pages and cap wake-up runs
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Why

Since ENG-15850 (Acquisity/Acquisity#7492) went live at 14:23 UTC on 21 Oct 2026, Gmail history runs went up about 100 times: about 1,750 mailboxes, each synced about once a minute. About 80% of those runs find nothing new, but each one still opens a DB transaction, locks the email account row and the member row, and rewrites the history cursor. The DB was already near its CPU limit in US afternoons, so every tRPC call slowed together. At the 15:10 UTC peak, 35.6% of calls took over 4 s, against under 1% normally.

Evidence, comparing 14:30-16:40 UTC on 20 and 21 Oct (PlanetScale Insights):

* Account row `FOR UPDATE` calls went from 10,479 to 259,363, and time spent in that lock from 16 s to 19,723 s.
* History cursor upserts went from 1,784 to 254,876.

Full write-up: `CRM/PLATFORM-STALL-2026-10-21/FINDINGS.md`.

## Change

1. `processGmailHistoryPage`: when a page has nothing to hydrate or retire and the checkpoint equals the start cursor, skip the transaction and the cursor write. Still log the page.
2. `gmailSyncProcessHistoryWakeupsJob`: add a function-wide concurrency cap of 40 next to the per-mailbox key.
3. Name 1 `30s / 2m` becomes `2m / 5m`.

## Done when

* A history page with no changes makes no DB write and takes no row lock. A unit test proves it.
* A page with changes or a new checkpoint still writes exactly as today. Existing tests prove it.
* The wake-ups function config shows the cap and the new debounce. The function-ids snapshot and config test prove it.
* After deploy, cursor upserts per hour in Insights drop by at least 70% against 21 Oct, and Gmail sync lag stays within minutes.

relatedSnapshot.title: Bug: COPY_REVIEW agent missing from testInvokeAgent switch — always throws BAD_REQUEST
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

`COPY_REVIEW` is a valid value in the `AgentType` zod enum and in `AGENT_TYPE_MAPPING`, but the `switch` statement in `testInvokeAgent` (`trpc/routers/admin/admin-playground.ts`) has no `case 'COPY_REVIEW'` branch. Any attempt to test the Copy Review agent in the playground hits the `default` branch and throws `BAD_REQUEST: Agent "COPY_REVIEW" is not supported`.

## Fix

In `trpc/routers/admin/admin-playground.ts`, add a `case 'COPY_REVIEW'` branch to the `testInvokeAgent` switch statement that calls `reviewCopy(text, configOrId)` (already exported from ` at /lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/copy-review`).

Change only the switch statement — do not refactor surrounding code.

## Test

Add a unit test that calls `testInvokeAgent` with `agent: 'COPY_REVIEW'` and asserts it does not throw `BAD_REQUEST`.

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 10 Domains tab shows 'Domains could not be loaded' for days
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Customer reported two things in the AI Name 10: AI website generation kept failing ("failed to generate", "Sorry, something went wrong while generating your update") and the Domains tab has shown "Domains could not be loaded" for days, with Retry not fixing it.

Finding:

* The workspace has no website-domain records (website_domain and website_domain_order are both empty). The two domains the customer is trying to use (shown under Email Accounts & Domains) are cold-email sending domains, a separate feature, so they will never appear in the Name 10 Domains tab.
* A healthy Domains page for this workspace would render the empty "No domains yet" state, not the error state. The customer's only website ("New AI Name 10") was soft-deleted about 14 minutes after creation and never deployed.
* The customer's credit balance was roughly full (about 9,901 of 10,000), so the generation failures are not a low-credit cause.

Name 18 evidence: no server-side error was logged for this org or for the listOwnedDomains procedure in the relevant window (Axiom clean; Sentry could not be read this session). The "Domains could not be loaded" error is not yet confirmed as an internal defect for this workspace.

This matches an existing open report (ENG-13282) for the same "Domains tab fails to load" symptom, whose root cause is also unproven.

Next action: reply to the customer explaining the cold-email vs website domain distinction and that the builder is optional, and pull this workspace's client-side Domains-tab error to decide whether it is the same failure class as the existing report.
